newsitem.title: USA: Argentine corruption comments not recorded - Cavallo.
newsitem.headline: Argentine corruption comments not recorded - Cavallo.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said on Tuesday his corruption charges against two key cabinet officials were based on private conversations for which no record existed.

Cavallo, architect of Argentina's economic stabilisation, had accused Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan earlier on Tuesday of manipulating judges and state prosecutors.
He said the two ministers had made self-incriminating comments, but he had no tape recordings or documentation of the conversations.

"It's my word against those of the two ministers," Cavallo told reporters at a New York University dinner here. "It's a question of credibility: do the people believe in what I say or in what they say."
Argentine President Carlos Menem responded to Cavallo's charges by challenging him to prove the claims in court.
Cavallo, who was sacked in July by Menem, was in New York to teach at NYU this academic year. He plans to run for the Argentina Congress next year.
"I just told the people about talks that we had with these two ministers," Cavallo said after the dinner.
"Talk cannot be documented. I did not make recordings."

The accusations that stunned Buenos Aires emerged when a local radio broadcast Cavallo's statements that Corach had tried to remove a judge from investigating a gold-export fraud case and replace him with another magistrate "who had failed to find any crime commited by gold exporters".
The former minister said that Corach once wrote on a paper napkin the name of several judges and state prosecutors and bragged: "These do as I say."
Jassan used to call judges and prosecutors to give them instructions on issues he was interested in, Cavallo said.
Corach rejected the charges, calling them "totally irresponsible and reflecting (Cavallo's) state of emotional imbalance". He also said he had issued instructions for immediate judicial action.
A spokesman for Jassan said the justice minister had no immediate plans to react to Cavallo's charges.
